caption:
Fig.1: Comparison of restoration paradigms. (a) All-in-one model: Uses
a single network with specialized heads to inject various degradation features. (b)
Training-free Agent: Uses VLMs for static task planning, executing sub-tasks se-
quentially via exhaustive tool traversal. (c) TIR-Agent (Ours): A trainable agent
that dynamically decides the next sub-task based on current results and learns to di-
rectly select the optimal tool, avoiding redundant execution.
delegated_acceptance_review: Viewed original, generated first attempt and final, read caption. Final restores source bird examples and all scientific panels. Six-degradation all-in-one route, static denoise/dehaze/deblur tools, Single Step Best/IQA pass-fail rollback, dynamic TIR initial plan and intermediate-state tool selection all remain. New headings and IQA expansion are caption-grounded; no invented new tool output or direction. First generated draft redrew original bird data and is retained as a repair predecessor.
